title: AI for multimodal learning and model quality
text: **A21 · Proposed multimodal research representation**

pages.title: A21 Multimodal representation learning
text: **A21 · Proposed multimodal research representation**

Multimodal representation learning combines information from different observation channels into features useful for a defined task. It can model relationships that are difficult to express manually. Its value depends on whether the channels add relevant information and whether their timing, calibration and missingness are understood.
## Demonstrate complementarity

A combined model should be compared with its strongest single-channel baseline. Removing each channel can reveal whether it contributes useful information or merely increases complexity. The evaluation should also challenge common-cause disturbances that can affect several channels at once.

The representation itself is not a biological result. Its downstream use must be defined and evaluated. A fused score should retain the original observations and their quality states so that a reviewer can investigate why the result changed after a sensor fault, configuration change or reprocessing. Unqualified signals should not gain credibility merely by entering a larger model.

pages.title: A22 Sensor disagreement detection
text: **A22 · Proposed disagreement and fault assessment**

Sensor disagreement detection identifies observations that are inconsistent with their expected relationship. AI may learn normal cross-channel patterns and highlight unusual residuals. The detected discrepancy can have several explanations, including a sensor fault, timing error, changed environment or an inadequate model.
## Disagreement does not identify the truth

If two channels disagree, the model should not automatically choose the one that resembles its training data. The investigation should consider calibration, timing, location and what each channel measures. A third channel helps only if it contributes sufficiently independent information.

The proposed output should support a defined recovery path. Some events may justify excluding a failed auxiliary sensor; others may invalidate the whole observation. These paths need separate evaluation. A system that detects a discrepancy but still releases the same unsupported conclusion has not achieved the intended error-reduction function.

pages.title: A23 Missing modality handling
text: **A23 · Proposed missing-data handling**

Missing-modality handling determines what analysis remains justified when one or more expected channels are unavailable. AI may support a qualified reduced-input model or a research imputation, but neither should be represented as if the missing sensor produced a real observation.
## Missingness has a cause

A channel absent because a sample is outside its range may contain different information from a channel absent because a cable disconnected. The model should not assume those events are equivalent. The original reason should remain part of the record.

For a clinical workflow, only separately qualified degraded modes should be eligible. Research imputation can be useful for model exploration or sensitivity analysis, but it should carry an imputed value type and a link to the method. It must not fill gaps in the original measured series or conceal that the biological observation was never acquired.

pages.title: A24 Out of distribution detection
text: **A24 · Proposed domain suitability assessment**

Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input differs materially from the domain in which a model was developed and evaluated. No detector can guarantee recognition of every unfamiliar case. Its role is to provide an additional signal for review and abstention, alongside explicit eligibility checks.
## Domain is more than appearance

A familiar-looking plate can still have an unsupported organism, drug, medium or reading time. Those conditions require explicit context checks. Conversely, an unfamiliar background may not affect the measurement if the relevant evidence remains qualified.

The proposed system should combine domain indicators with task-specific quality assessment. Evaluation should include new sites, instruments, vessel types and workflow conditions without using them to tune the detector after seeing the final test results. A novelty score should be explained through its tested operational meaning, not presented as a universal measure of biological uncertainty.

pages.title: A25 Confidence calibration
text: **A25 · Proposed confidence calibration**

Confidence calibration examines whether a model’s stated confidence corresponds to observed performance. A model can rank easy and difficult cases well while still assigning misleading probabilities. Calibration should be evaluated separately from discrimination and should remain specific to the task and population.
## Confidence is not a permission rule by itself

A high calibrated probability still needs to be interpreted against the consequence of error, the intended use and the availability of review. A low-confidence output may require another observation or an established alternative workflow.

Calibration should be reassessed when the model, acquisition pipeline or data distribution changes materially. The record should identify the calibration method and dataset version. A display should avoid false precision: a percentage with several decimal places does not communicate more useful certainty if the supporting evaluation is limited. The purpose is an empirically meaningful uncertainty statement that helps the user make an appropriate decision.

pages.title: A26 Active data selection
text: **A26 · Proposed data acquisition support**

Active data selection prioritizes examples that may be useful for improving a model or resolving a known evidence gap. AI can identify uncertainty, diversity or disagreement patterns, but its selection can also bias the resulting dataset. A representative evaluation set must remain independent of that process.
## Preserve the sampling story

A dataset enriched for difficult cases is useful for development but may not estimate routine prevalence or workflow performance. Its selection policy should therefore accompany the data. Researchers should be able to reconstruct why a record entered the training set.

The proposed function should support expert-led collection decisions rather than autonomously expand data use. Privacy, consent and partner permissions still apply. A model should not request patient-linked data merely because an uncertainty score is high. The collection plan should identify the minimum information needed to answer the development question and maintain separate evaluation data for the final claim.

pages.title: A27 Annotation quality assistance
text: **A27 · Proposed annotation quality assistance**

Annotation assistance identifies potentially inconsistent, incomplete or difficult labels for human review. AI may compare annotations with image features or with related records. Its role is to surface questions, not to replace independent reference labels with the model’s preferred answer.
## Avoid circular ground truth

If a model’s prediction becomes the label used to evaluate the same model, apparent agreement can improve without any improvement in truth. The annotation process should preserve who saw which information and when. Blinded review is important where it supports the selected evaluation design.

The proposed interface should present the original evidence, competing annotations and the relevant instructions. An adjudicator should be able to retain uncertainty rather than being forced to choose a precise value. Quality assistance succeeds when it improves the reliability and transparency of the reference process, not when it makes the dataset look more consistent with the current model.

pages.title: A28 Dataset shift monitoring
text: **A28 · Proposed distribution monitoring**

Dataset shift monitoring tracks changes in the observations or populations encountered by a deployed or research system. AI may summarize complex image or feature distributions, while explicit metadata can reveal changes in instruments, sites or workflows. A detected shift does not automatically mean performance has degraded.
## Connect an alert to a review process

The proposed response should identify who investigates, what additional evidence is needed and whether any workflow restriction is justified. Automatic retraining should not be the default reaction, because it can introduce new unvalidated behaviour.

Monitoring should preserve privacy and site context. Aggregated statistics may support an investigation without transferring patient-linked records. Changes in data availability or review practice can also alter monitored distributions and should be recorded. The objective is early recognition of a meaningful change and a controlled response, not an uninterrupted stream of novelty alerts.

pages.title: A29 Sequence quality triage
text: **A29 · Proposed sequence-data triage**

Sequence quality triage helps determine whether molecular data are suitable for a proposed downstream analysis. AI may identify complex quality patterns, but established pipeline checks and explicit metadata should remain central. The task concerns the quality of measured sequence data, not inference of a sequence from a plate image.
## Preserve the molecular provenance

The record should retain accession or file identity, tool versions, reference data and the quality decisions made. A later database or pipeline update should produce a new analysis version. NCBI documentation provides a basis for understanding the context and limitations of its sequence-based resources. [R25]

This proposed capability belongs to the bioinformatics product track. It should not silently reject or alter measured molecular data. Where quality is insufficient, the output should identify the limitation and the analysis it affects, allowing a qualified user to decide whether additional evidence or a different workflow is required.

pages.title: A30 Resistance gene evidence retrieval
text: **A30 · Proposed resistance-evidence analysis**

Resistance-gene evidence retrieval connects qualified molecular observations with curated knowledge about resistance determinants. The function may combine sequence-analysis outputs with structured evidence retrieval. It should preserve the distinction between a detected sequence feature, a database annotation and a clinically expressed phenotype.
## Keep the evidence chain visible

CARD and NCBI resources offer different forms of resistance-related information. The proposed system should identify the resource and version used, the analysis method and the exact molecular input. It should not describe a database hit as a new laboratory measurement. [R24] [R25]

The initial role is research and qualified molecular-result support. An absent match does not prove susceptibility, and a present determinant does not by itself establish every clinical consequence. The interface should preserve these limits and direct discrepancies to review rather than resolving them through an unsupported single confidence score.
